name: Fork
mnemonic: One piece, two targets — they can only save one.
definition: A single piece attacks two or more enemy pieces at once. Knights are the classic forkers because their attack can't be blocked.
hint: Which square does the knight attack with check and also hit a rook?
explanation: Ne7+ checks the king and attacks the c8-rook at the same time. The e1-rook protects the knight, so after the king steps away White takes the rook — a rook for a knight (winning the exchange).

extra.hint: Find a queen check that also hits a8.
extra.explanation: Qd5+ checks along the diagonal to g8 and at the same time attacks the a8-rook along the other diagonal. The queen forks in two directions.
e5 attacks the d6-bishop and the f6-knight at once, and the d4-pawn protects it. Black can save only one piece.

name: Pin
mnemonic: Frozen in place: moving would expose something bigger.
definition: A piece cannot move (or moving it would lose more) because a more valuable piece stands behind it on the same line. An absolute pin is against the king.
hint: Line up a bishop with the queen and the king on the long diagonal.
explanation: Bd4 pins the f6-queen to the h8-king along the a1–h8 diagonal. The queen can't step off the line, so the best Black can do is give it up for the bishop.

extra.hint: The knight cannot move — attack it.
extra.explanation: The e5-knight is pinned to the king by the e1-rook. f4 attacks it with a pawn, and the pinned knight can't escape: White wins a knight for a pawn.

name: Skewer
mnemonic: A pin in reverse: the big piece is in front and must move.
definition: A line piece attacks a valuable piece, which must move and expose a piece behind it on the same line.
hint: Check the king along the 7th rank.
explanation: Ra7+ attacks the king; once it steps off the 7th rank, the rook runs through to h7 and takes the queen standing behind it.

extra.hint: Check the king along the diagonal that leads to g8.
extra.explanation: Bc4+ checks the king on the c4–g8 diagonal. Once the king steps aside, the bishop takes the rook standing behind it.

name: Discovered attack
mnemonic: Move the curtain, reveal the gun.
definition: Moving one piece uncovers an attack by another piece behind it. Best when the moving piece also makes a threat — then the opponent faces two at once.
hint: The bishop stands between your rook and Black's queen.
explanation: Bxh7+ gives check, uncovering the d1-rook against the d6-queen. Black must answer the check, and the queen falls.

extra.hint: The knight blocks your bishop's diagonal. Move it with check.
extra.explanation: Nf5+ is check, and it uncovers the b2-bishop against the h8-queen. Black must answer the check, so the queen falls.

name: Double check
mnemonic: Two checks at once: the king must run.
definition: A discovered check where the moving piece also gives check. No block or capture can stop both checks, so the king must move — often into mate.
hint: Sacrifice the queen to drag the king onto the d-file.
explanation: Réti–Tartakower, Vienna 1910. Qd8+!! forces Kxd8; then Bg5+ is a double check from the bishop and the d1-rook. After Kc7, Bd8# finishes.

name: Deflection
mnemonic: Pull the guard away from its post.
definition: Force a defending piece away from the square or piece it protects, usually with a check or capture it must answer.
hint: The d8-rook is the queen's only defender. Give it something else to do.
explanation: Re8+ forces Rxe8 because there is no escape square. The rook is deflected from the d-file, so White's queen captures the undefended queen on d5.

extra.hint: The c8-rook guards the queen. Give it a reason to leave.
extra.explanation: Re8+ must be answered by Rxe8 — the king has no square. The rook leaves the c-file, and the a3-queen takes the undefended queen on c5.

name: Decoy
mnemonic: Lure the piece onto a poisoned square.
definition: A sacrifice that draws an enemy piece (often the king) onto a square where it can be hit by another tactic.
hint: Get the king onto h8, where a knight check can also hit d6.
explanation: Rh8+! decoys the king to h8. Now Nxf7+ forks king and queen, and White comes out a queen for a rook ahead.

extra.hint: Lure the king to f8, where a knight can check it and hit b6.
extra.explanation: Rf8+! forces Kxf8 (every other square is covered). Now Nd7+ forks the king on f8 and the queen on b6 — a rook for a queen.

name: Overloading
mnemonic: One defender, two jobs — it can't do both.
definition: A defending piece has more than one duty. Attack one of its charges and the other collapses.
hint: The c8-rook guards both the bishop and the back rank.
explanation: The c8-rook defends the c6-bishop and the d8 square. Qxc6! forces it to choose: if Rxc6, Rd8 is mate on the undefended back rank.

extra.hint: The f6-knight guards both d7 and h7.
extra.explanation: The knight on f6 has two jobs: protect the d7-bishop and guard h7. Rxd7! — if Nxd7, the knight has left h7 and Qxh7 is mate (the b1-bishop backs up the queen).

name: Interference
mnemonic: Block the line between a defender and what it defends.
definition: Place a piece on the line between an enemy piece and the square it protects, cutting the connection.
hint: The h8-rook guards c8 along the 8th rank. Get in its way.
explanation: Rd8! interrupts the h8-rook's control of c8. If Black captures, cxd8=Q promotes with a capture; if not, c8=Q comes next.

name: Zwischenzug
mnemonic: Before you recapture, look for a check.
definition: An 'in-between move': instead of the expected recapture, play a forcing move first (usually a check), then recapture.
goal: Win a pawn and the right to castle
hint: Black's queen isn't going anywhere — it's trapped on d1.
explanation: Black just took on d1. Rxd1 at once is natural, but Bxf7+ first grabs a pawn with check and drags the king into the open; the queen on d1 is still there to be taken.

name: Removing the defender
mnemonic: Kill the guard, take the castle.
definition: Capture or drive away the piece that defends a key square or piece.
hint: Only the f6-knight stops Qxh7 mate.
explanation: The queen and c2-bishop aim at h7, defended only by the f6-knight. Bxf6 removes it, and whatever Black recaptures with, Qxh7 is mate.

extra.explanation: Only the f6-knight defends the d5-bishop. Bxf6 removes it, and after the recapture Rxd5 wins a piece.

name: X-ray
mnemonic: Power passes through pieces on the same line.
definition: A piece attacks or defends a square through another piece on the same line. When the front piece is exchanged, the one behind takes over.
hint: Your rook on d1 is behind your queen on the d-file.
explanation: The d1-rook 'sees through' the queen to d8. Qxd8+ Rxd8 removes the defender, and the rook recaptures with back-rank mate.

extra.hint: Your two rooks work as one on the e-file.
extra.explanation: The e1-rook sees through the e2-rook. Rxe8+ Qxe8 and the back rook recaptures with mate — two attackers beat one defender.

name: Windmill
mnemonic: Check, capture, check, capture — the sails keep turning.
definition: A rook (or other piece) alternates between direct checks and discovered checks, grabbing material on every second move.
hint: The f6-bishop gives check every time the rook leaves g7.
explanation: Each time the rook leaves g7, the bishop gives a discovered check; each time it returns, the rook checks directly. Rxf7+, Rg7+ and Rxc7+ grab a pawn and then the queen.

name: Back-rank mate
mnemonic: No luft, no life: a king walled in by its own pawns.
definition: A rook or queen mates a king on its first rank whose escape is blocked by its own pawns.
hint: The b8-rook is the only guard of the back rank.
explanation: Qe8+! forces the rook to capture, and Rxe8 is mate because f7, g7 and h7 imprison the king. Always consider making 'luft' (h6 or g6) in time.

extra.explanation: Black's own pawns on f7, g7 and h7 imprison the king, and no black piece can reach d8 or block on e8/f8. Rd8 is mate despite Black's extra material.

name: Scholar's mate
mnemonic: Queen and bishop gang up on f7 — the square only the king defends.
definition: The four-move mate on f7. Every beginner must know it — to deliver it and, more importantly, to stop it with ...Qe7, ...g6 or ...Nf6 at the right moment.
hint: Two white pieces aim at f7.
explanation: Black's 3...Nf6?? attacks the queen but ignores the threat. Qxf7 is mate: the bishop protects the queen and the king has no escape. 3...g6 or 3...Qe7 would have defended.

name: Smothered mate
mnemonic: A king buried by its own pieces dies to a lone knight.
definition: A knight mates a king that is surrounded by its own pieces. The classic finish is a queen sacrifice on g8 that forces a rook to block the last flight square.
hint: Start with a double check from the knight and queen.
explanation: Nh6+ is a double check (knight and the d5-queen), so the king must go to h8. Qg8+!! forces Rxg8, and Nf7 is mate — the king is smothered by its own rook and pawns.

name: Arabian mate
mnemonic: Knight on f6, rook on h7 — the corner becomes a coffin.
definition: A rook and knight mate a king in the corner: the rook gives check next to the king and the knight both protects it and covers the escape square.
hint: The knight on f6 guards h7 and g8.
explanation: Rxh7 is mate: the rook is protected by the f6-knight, which also covers g8; g7 is blocked by Black's own pawn.

name: Anastasia's mate
mnemonic: Knight on e7 walls off g6 and g8; the rook finishes on the h-file.
definition: A knight on e7 (or e2) takes the king's flight squares while a rook or queen mates along the edge file. Often prepared with a queen sacrifice on h7.
hint: Sacrifice the queen to open the h-file.
explanation: Qxh7+! drags the king to h7; Rh3 is mate because the e7-knight covers g8 and g6 and the g7-pawn blocks the last square.

name: Boden's mate
mnemonic: Two bishops on criss-crossing diagonals catch a long-castled king.
definition: Two bishops mate a king (usually castled long) along crossing diagonals, while the king's own pieces block its escape.
hint: Remove the b7-pawn's protection of the a6–c8 diagonal.
explanation: Qxc6+! forces bxc6, opening the a6–c8 diagonal. Ba6 is mate: the f4-bishop covers b8 and c7, and Black's own rook and knight block d8 and d7.

name: Greek gift (Bxh7+)
mnemonic: Bishop takes h7, knight to g5, queen to h5.
definition: The classic bishop sacrifice on h7 (or h2). It works when White has a pawn on e5 (no ...Nf6 defence), a knight ready for g5 and a queen that can reach h5.
hint: The h7-pawn is defended only by the king.
explanation: Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ Kg8 Qh5 threatens Qh7 mate, and Black has no knight on f6 to defend (the e5-pawn controls that square). Check the three conditions — e5-pawn, Ng5, Qh5 — before sacrificing. 2...Kg6 is the toughest defence.

name: Ladder mate (two rooks)
mnemonic: One rook cuts, the other checks — climb the ladder to the edge.
definition: Two rooks (or queen and rook) take turns: one guards a rank, the other checks on the next rank, pushing the king to the edge.
hint: Rook a4 already guards the 4th rank.
explanation: Each rook check pushes the king one rank up while the other rook guards the rank behind it. Keep the rooks far from the king so it can't attack them.

name: Discovered check
mnemonic: The piece that moves can grab anything — the check comes from behind.
definition: Moving a piece uncovers a check from another piece. Because the opponent must answer the check, the moving piece can capture or attack whatever it likes.
hint: Your rook on e1 is aimed at the black king.
explanation: Bxa8+ takes the queen and uncovers check from the e1-rook. Black must deal with the check and can never recapture.

name: Trapped piece
mnemonic: Before you grab, count the escape squares.
definition: A piece with no safe squares can be won by attacking it. Bishops that grab pawns on a2/h2 (or a7/h7) are classic victims.
hint: Shut the bishop in with a pawn.
explanation: After b3 the a2-bishop has no squares: b1 and b3 are covered by the king. Black can only give it up for a pawn.

name: Underpromotion
mnemonic: A queen isn't always best — a knight can fork with check.
definition: Promoting to a knight (or rook/bishop) when it gives check, forks, or avoids stalemate.
hint: Black threatens ...Qxh2 mate. You need a promotion with check.
explanation: e8=Q? allows ...Qxh2 mate. e8=N+! promotes with check and forks the king and the c7-queen — White wins the queen and the threat disappears.

name: Pawn breakthrough
mnemonic: Three against three: sacrifice the middle pawn and one gets through.
definition: Pawn sacrifices that force a passed pawn through a blockade — decisive when the enemy king is too far away.
hint: Push the middle pawn first.
explanation: b6! If axb6, c6! bxc6 a6 and the a-pawn queens; if cxb6, a6! bxa6 c6. Black's king is too far away to help.
